title: How I Budget on a $41k Salary (Real Numbers, No Shame)
creator: Priya Talks Money
description:
My actual budget for October: rent, groceries, the car, savings, and the fun money I refuse to give up.

I use Tallyway to track everything. Try it free for 60 days with code PRIYA60 at tallyway.com/priya

Free budget template: priyatalksmoney.com/template
I'm not a financial advisor, this is just what works for me.

sentences.t: Hi friends, so a lot of you asked me to show my real budget, with real numbers, so that's what we're doing today.
I make forty one thousand a year before tax, I live in Columbus, and I'm going to show you every single dollar from October.
After taxes and my retirement contribution, my take-home is about twenty seven hundred a month.
Rent is the big one, it's nine hundred and fifty, and I have a roommate, which is how it's that low.
Some people say I'm too old for roommates, and to those people I say, have you seen rent?
So the way I actually track all this is in Tallyway, and I'll just pull it up on screen so you can see.
Every transaction from my checking account and my credit card comes in automatically, and I go through them every Sunday with a coffee.
See this one, it marked a Target run as groceries, but half of it was a lamp, so I'm just going to split it, sixty dollars groceries, forty home stuff.
And this little bar at the top shows me I've spent two eighty out of my three hundred grocery budget, with four days to go.
So that's a little tight, which tells me this week is pasta week.
I've also got a rule set up, anything from the gas station near my work automatically goes into the car category, so I don't have to touch those.
And when I scroll down, here's the whole month as a pie chart, rent, car, groceries, savings, and that sad little slice called fun.
Okay, so fun money, let's talk about it.
Oh, and before I forget, Tallyway is actually sponsoring this video, which I was really excited about because I've used it for two years.
If you want to try it, you get sixty days free with my code PRIYA60, and the link is right down in the description.
That's tallyway dot com slash priya, it works with pretty much every bank, and you can cancel any time.
Alright, fun money.
I give myself a hundred and fifty a month, and I don't feel guilty about any of it.
In October that was a concert, two dinners out with friends, and a very ugly sweater I'm wearing right now.
The car is the next big one, my payment is two hundred and ten, insurance is a hundred and five, and gas is usually around a hundred.
I know a lot of finance people say never have a car payment, but there's no real bus to my job, so this is a need, not a want.
Then savings, I put three hundred a month into a high yield savings account, automatically, the day after I get paid.
That's my emergency fund, and it's at about four months of expenses right now, which is the most I've ever had.
The rest is phone, internet, a couple of subscriptions, and a little buffer for things I always forget, like birthday presents.
So all in, I end most months with somewhere between fifty and a hundred dollars left over.
That's not a lot, I know.
But two years ago I was ending every month negative and putting groceries on a credit card, so this feels like a big deal to me.
If you're in a similar spot, start with tracking, honestly, before you change anything.
Just look at where it goes for a month, no judgment, and the patterns will jump out at you.
Let me know in the comments what your biggest category is, I'm nosy.
And I'll see you in the next one.
